hints: Focus on the word systole. It means contraction, so picture the thick muscular walls of the ventricles squeezing hard on the blood inside.
Think pressure first, then valves. When ventricles squeeze, does their pressure rise or fall, and which valves must shut and which must open to push blood out into the aorta?
walkthrough:
**Remember what ventricular systole means**

Think of systole as a squeeze. The ventricles contract, so the volume inside gets smaller and the pressure on the blood gets bigger.

Key idea:
$$ventricular \ contraction \rightarrow ventricular \ pressure \ rises$$

**Follow the valves from pressure**

High ventricular pressure slams the atrioventricular valves shut to stop backflow to the atria. Once ventricular pressure is higher than pressure in the aorta and pulmonary artery, the semilunar valves are forced open.

**Link ejection to aortic pressure**

With semilunar valves open, blood is ejected into the aorta. Adding that volume of blood into the aorta raises aortic pressure. That is why A is the only correct description.

options.A: Correct. Ejection of blood from the left ventricle into the aorta during ventricular systole increases aortic pressure.
options.B: False. Rising ventricular pressure closes the atrioventricular valves to prevent backflow, they do not open until diastole.
options.C: False. The semilunar valves open during ventricular systole to allow ejection, they close later when ventricles relax.
options.D: False. Contraction of the ventricular muscle increases ventricular pressure, it does not decrease it.
